subject: Dedicated GPU projection: TradeCraft PoC throughput & SLO headroom
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@tradecraft.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity projection for PoC

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for the demo last week. TradeCraft is moving forward with a 6-week PoC and we need a short capacity projection so our CTO and procurement can sign off. High-level details below:

- Expected users for PoC: 8,000 MAU (focused on power users)
- Peak concurrent sessions (estimate): 120–160 concurrent streams during US morning peak
- Typical prompt + generation size: ~60 tokens prompt, ~120 tokens generation (we're assuming ~180 tokens total per request)
- SLO: p95 response time <= 800 ms for user-facing completions; offline jobs tolerate higher latency
- Target model: prefer a ~13B-class open model (we're flexible — want cost + latency tradeoff)

Can you provide tokens/sec estimates, recommended GPU count for a Dedicated pool (with 30–40% headroom), and any quantization/batching recommendations that affect TCO?

Also include any procurement lead times and recommended canary plan.

Best,
Natalie Chen
Head of AI Products, TradeCraft

Attachments: tradecraft_usage_forecast.xlsx (forecast, anonymized)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@tradecraft.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-16T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity projection for PoC

Hi Natalie — looping in Karthik (SE) and Rishi (Solutions) to provide the sizing math. Quick prelim notes while they run numbers:

- Using your numbers (avg ~180 tokens / request) and a p95 target of 800 ms, we model request/sec as concurrency / latency. At 140 concurrent / 0.8s -> ~175 req/s.
- Tokens/sec needed = 175 req/s * 180 tokens = ~31,500 tokens/sec peak.
- For a 13B-class quantized model (8-bit Q8 with KV cache), our benchmark on an A100-80GB equivalent shows ~4,000–5,500 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and batching.
- Conservative baseline: assume 4,250 tokens/sec per GPU -> baseline GPUs = ceil(31,500 / 4,250) = 8 GPUs.
- Adding 35% headroom for bursts, autoscaling latency cushion, and progressive rollouts -> ~11 GPUs reserved.

Karthik / Rishi — please attach the detailed calc and call out batching assumptions (e.g., target batch size 8–12, expected KV cache hit from repeated prompts, and effects of 2-token sampling steps).

I'll follow up with a formal PDF and timeline.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie@tradecraft.ai>
Date: 2025-08-17T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity projection for PoC

Folks — attaching the detailed calc (tradecraft_capacity_calc.xlsx). Summary of modeling assumptions and sensitive levers:

1) Workload assumptions (from Natalie / forecast):
   - Peak concurrency used for calc: 140 (midpoint of provided range)
   - p95 target latency: 800ms (end-to-end serving time — not including network)
   - Avg tokens/request: 180 total (prompt + generated)

2) Throughput math (conservative):
   - req/s = concurrency / latency = 140 / 0.8 = 175 req/s
   - tokens/sec = 175 * 180 = 31,500 t/s

3) Per-GPU profiles (13B quantized, mixed precision, KV cache warm):
   - Measured median: 4,800 t/s (batching 10, seq=180)
   - Measured p95 degradation at high concurrency: ~15% drop -> use 4,080 t/s for planning

4) Hidden optimizations to reclaim headroom:
   - Prefix/KV caching expected to hit ~20% on repeated prompts -> effective load reduction ~12%
   - Dynamic batching with 50–150ms window historically gains 25% throughput in our infra

5) Recommended Dedicated pool sizes:
   - Minimum reserve to meet p95 with minimal headroom: ceil(31,500 / 4,080) = 8 GPUs
   - Recommended reserve with 35% operational headroom: ceil(31,500 * 1.35 / 4,080) = 11 GPUs
   - Suggested burst pool (on Shared / Dedicated burst): +3 GPUs available for rare spikes
6) SLO fit notes and mitigations:
   - If you need tighter p95 (<= 500ms), plan to double GPUs or move to a lower-latency model family; or use a hybrid routing with smaller model for short completions.
   - We recommend canary ramp: Week 1: 2 GPUs (smoke), Week 2: 4 GPUs (limited users), Week 3: 8 GPUs (broad) then switch to reserved 11 with autoscale policies
7) Procurement & lead time:
   - Dedicated pool provisioning (internal) typically 3–5 business days after contract; on-prem/VPC options may add 2–4 weeks for networking/KMS
Notes: the calc spreadsheet breaks down token-per-second per GPU by seq length and batch windows. We'll also include a PDF summary for your procurement team.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: tradecraft_capacity_calc.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Chen <natalie@tradecraft.ai>, TradeCraft Procurement <procurement@tradecraft.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-20T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood PoC capacity proposal (summary + next steps)

Hi Natalie / TradeCraft team —

Attached is a short PDF summary of the PoC capacity recommendation (redwood-poc-capacity-proposal.pdf) and a one-page rollout plan. Key bullets:

- Recommended Reserved Dedicated pool: 11 GPUs (13B-class, Q8) to meet p95 <= 800ms with ~35% headroom
- Suggested burst policy: +3 GPUs from shared capacity for infrequent peaks
- Canary ramp: 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 11 over three weeks, with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if p95 exceeds threshold during rollout
- Cost note: quantization + batching expected to reduce per-token cost by ~22% vs FP16 baseline; we'll publish a line-item estimate in the contract appendix

Please review and tell us your preferred procurement date. Once we have sign-off we can provision the Dedicated pool and share a DocuSign link for the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
- TradeCraft signs SOW for PoC capacity (we'll provide DocuSign)
- Week of 8/25: provisioning and canary setup
- Week of 9/1: full PoC launch

Thanks — attaching the PDF and the detailed calc again for your team.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-poc-capacity-proposal.pdf, tradecraft_capacity_calc.xlsx, docsign-tradecraft-poc.docx
From: Natalie Chen <natalie@tradecraft.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: TradeCraft Procurement <procurement@tradecraft.ai>
Date: 2025-08-21T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood PoC capacity proposal (summary + next steps)

Hi Monica —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail our CTO was asking for. A few quick follow-ups:

- Procurement wants the DocuSign SOW and a line-item monthly estimate for the Dedicated pool (11 GPUs) vs a consumption model. Can you share the brief cost appendix?
- Can you confirm the autoscale policy defaults (cooldown window, max burst) so our infra can map firewall rules?
- We want to lock provisioning for the week of 8/25 if possible.

I'll route the PDF to legal and procurement today. If you can send DocuSign and the cost appendix by EOD tomorrow that will keep us on track.

Appreciate it —
Natalie
Head of AI Products, TradeCraft
